[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"JavaScript Operators: A Comprehensive Guide"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Operators are fundamental building blocks in JavaScript, allowing you to perform various operations on values (operands). This tutorial covers arithmetic, comparison, logical, and assignment operators, providing a solid foundation for writing effective JavaScript code."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Arithmetic Operators"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Arithmetic operators perform mathematical calculations. Here's a breakdown:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"+ (Addition): Adds two operands. Example: 5 + 2 = 7"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"- (Subtraction): Subtracts the second operand from the first. Example: 5 - 2 = 3"},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"* (Multiplication): Multiplies two operands. Example: 5 * 2 = 10"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"/ (Division): Divides the first operand by the second. Example: 5 / 2 = 2.5"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"% (Modulus): Returns the remainder of a division operation. Example: 5 % 2 = 1"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"** (Exponentiation): Raises the first operand to the power of the second. Example: 5 ** 2 = 25"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"++ (Increment): Increases the operand by 1. Can be used as prefix (++x) or postfix (x++)."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-- (Decrement): Decreases the operand by 1. Can be used as prefix (--x) or postfix (x--)."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"// Example of arithmetic operators
let x = 5;
let y = 2;

console.log(x + y); // Output: 7
console.log(x - y); // Output: 3
console.log(x * y); // Output: 10
console.log(x / y); // Output: 2.5
console.log(x % y); // Output: 1
console.log(x ** y); // Output: 25
console.log(++x);   // Output: 6 (x is now 6)
console.log(y--);   // Output: 2 (y is now 1)"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Comparison Operators"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Comparison operators compare two operands and return a boolean value (true or false)."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"== (Equal to): Checks if two operands are equal in value (type coercion may occur). Example: 5 == '5' is true."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"=== (Strict equal to): Checks if two operands are equal in value and type. Example: 5 === '5' is false."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"!= (Not equal to): Checks if two operands are not equal in value (type coercion may occur). Example: 5 != '5' is false."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"!== (Strict not equal to): Checks if two operands are not equal in value or type. Example: 5 !== '5' is true."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"> (Greater than): Checks if the first operand is greater than the second. Example: 5 > 2 is true."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"< (Less than): Checks if the first operand is less than the second. Example: 5 < 2 is false."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":">= (Greater than or equal to): Checks if the first operand is greater than or equal to the second. Example: 5 >= 5 is true."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"<= (Less than or equal to): Checks if the first operand is less than or equal to the second. Example: 5 <= 5 is true."},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"// Example of comparison operators
let x = 5;
let y = '5';

console.log(x == y);  // Output: true
console.log(x === y); // Output: false
console.log(x != y);  // Output: false
console.log(x !== y); // Output: true
console.log(x > 2);   // Output: true
console.log(x < 2);   // Output: false
console.log(x >= 5);  // Output: true
console.log(x <= 5);  // Output: true"},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Logical Operators"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Logical operators combine or modify boolean expressions."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"&& (Logical AND): Returns true if both operands are true. Example: (5 > 2) && (3 < 6) is true."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"|| (Logical OR): Returns true if at least one operand is true. Example: (5 > 2) || (3 > 6) is true."},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"! (Logical NOT): Returns the opposite of the operand's boolean value. Example: !(5 > 2) is false."},{"order":30,"type":"code","text":"// Example of logical operators
let x = 5;
let y = 2;

console.log((x > y) && (x < 10)); // Output: true
console.log((x > y) || (x > 10)); // Output: true
console.log(!(x > y));          // Output: false"},{"order":31,"type":"subheading","text":"Assignment Operators"},{"order":32,"type":"paragraph","text":"Assignment operators assign values to variables."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"= (Assignment): Assigns the value of the right operand to the left operand. Example: x = 5"},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"+= (Addition assignment): Adds the right operand to the left operand and assigns the result to the left operand. Example: x += 5 (equivalent to x = x + 5)"},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-= (Subtraction assignment): Subtracts the right operand from the left operand and assigns the result to the left operand. Example: x -= 5 (equivalent to x = x - 5)"},{"order":36,"type":"*= (Multiplication assignment): Multiplies the left operand by the right operand and assigns the result to the left operand. Example: x *= 5 (equivalent to x = x * 5)"},{"order":37,"type":"bullet_point","text":"/= (Division assignment): Divides the left operand by the right operand and assigns the result to the left operand. Example: x /= 5 (equivalent to x = x / 5)"},{"order":38,"type":"bullet_point","text":"%= (Modulus assignment): Calculates the modulus of the left operand by the right operand and assigns the result to the left operand. Example: x %= 5 (equivalent to x = x % 5)"},{"order":39,"type":"**= (Exponentiation assignment): Raises the left operand to the power of the right operand and assigns the result to the left operand. Example: x **= 5 (equivalent to x = x ** 5)"},{"order":40,"type":"code","text":"// Example of assignment operators
let x = 10;

x += 5; // x is now 15
console.log(x); // Output: 15

x -= 3; // x is now 12
console.log(x); // Output: 12

x *= 2; // x is now 24
console.log(x); // Output: 24

x /= 4; // x is now 6
console.log(x); // Output: 6

x %= 5; // x is now 1
console.log(x); // Output: 1

x **= 3; // x is now 1
console.log(x); // Output: 1"},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding and utilizing these operators effectively is crucial for writing robust and efficient JavaScript code. Remember to consider operator precedence and type coercion when working with different data types."}]
